rust_summary: damage a mod can change once armour took its share, and hear once it reached the health (`native_living_damage_pre`, `native_living_damage_post`).
doc_summary:
damage a mod can change once the reductions took their share (`native_living_damage_pre`, NeoForge's
`LivingDamageEvent.Pre`) and hear once it reached the health (`native_living_damage_post`, `LivingDamageEvent.Post`): in
`LivingEntity.actuallyHurt`, the first after the armour, the enchantments and Resistance and before absorption, the second at
the end, after the health was set and before a death the hit caused is handled. Both name the hurt entity (its id and type,
`minecraft:player` for a player) and the hit's damage source as `native_living_incoming_damage` does. A mod may change
`amount` in the first: absorption, then the health, take what it leaves, and 0 hurts nothing; a value that is not a finite
number is put back as it was and one below 0 is 0. The second hears what reached the health (0 when absorption took it
all), once for each hit the first was told of. Neither is told of a hit the game stopped before (canceled by
`native_living_incoming_damage`, inside the invulnerable time and no stronger than the last, a mob's that Resistance took
whole), nor of what a wolf's armour takes. They have no `self`: the game is in the middle of the hit. They run on the
thread that ticks the world, so state a mod shares with its render thread hooks needs synchronising.

Bundles that use them need `"hooks": @API:living_damage@`.
